title: Statically determinate frame: displacements caused by support settlements

source.work: Bentley Systems, STAAD.Pro Help, Verification Examples (public documentation, docs.bentley.com)
source.edition: STAAD.Pro Help v21 build (pages refer to the STAAD.Pro 2023 sample files), read 2026-11-22
source.notes: problem statement taken from the vendor page (text and input listing). The page cites: C. K. Wang, Intermediate Structural Analysis, 1983, section 2.11, p. 47 - NOT opened for this project; no number is taken from it. The page's 'theory' values are recorded as printed; the program's own results are not used.

analysis: Plane problem in the global X-Y plane (Y vertical); the out-of-plane DOFs (uz, rx, ry) of every node are held; in-plane bending about local z. Frame with nodes A (0, 0), B (0, 7.5 m), C (6 m, 7.5 m), D (6 m, 2.5 m); A pinned, D on a roller that holds the vertical displacement only. Members AB and CD: A = 2400 cm^2, I = 720,000 cm^4; BC: A = 4800 cm^2, I = 1.44e6 cm^4; E = 2171.84 kN/cm^2. Load case 1: support A settles 1 cm; load case 2: support D settles 1 cm. The frame is statically determinate: the displacements are a rigid-body motion. The page works in kN and cm; the model file is in kN and mm (the input format has no cm). Reference values: computed here from this statement (verification/derive/vendor_reference.py); the textbook cited by the vendor page was not opened and no number is taken from it.

quarantine.diagnosis: All 12 displacement targets are reproduced (largest relative difference 2.0e-4, inside the printed precision), but the model cannot pass tiers C, D and E, so the problem stays quarantined. Cause: the frame is statically determinate, so a support settlement produces a rigid-body motion with NO member forces and NO reactions. Every force of the solution is round-off of zero (largest member end force or moment 1.3e-8 in kN and mm, largest reaction 2e-12 kN), and the checks that compare forces relative to the largest force of the model then compare one rounding error with another: tier C reports the end moments of the engine and of PyNite as differing by 1.7 and 1.8 (relative) and the OpenSees route fails its own joint equilibrium check with a residual of order one; tier D reports station forces that differ from the end forces by 6e-4 to 4e-3; the member-split check of tier E is above its tolerance. None of these numbers says anything about the displacements, and none shows an error of the engine or of a foreign solver. The reference solution (plane frame program of verification/derive/vendor_reference.py) gives the rigid-body displacements the page prints (1.25 cm, 0.001667 rad, 0.4167 cm) with forces of 1e-12 kN. History: an earlier build of the engine refused this model ('invariant failed'), for the same reason inside its own invariants; a round-off floor on the force scales of the invariants removed that refusal (docs/THEORY.md 8.1). The verification tiers were not changed to let the problem through, and no load was added to the model to make its forces non-zero.
